analysis:
Examined base text of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py lines 1-869, an offline unittest of the CI workflow structure, plus the head patch excerpt.

In the head, VALIDATE_GIT (head lines 152-187) tightens checks on a restored cached .git before git reads it. It discards a symlinked or non-directory .git, any symlink inside it, non-sample hooks matched case-insensitively, and config or config.worktree files that set core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or include/includeIf. It then keeps the existing fsck connectivity check. This hardens the CI supply chain against a poisoned Actions cache running code, so it is not a regression.

The head also adds a CACHE_GATE_STEP, which sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off on Darkbloom sandboxes that have no Darkbloom cache. It also changes the conditions on cache save and restore steps (base lines 635 and 639-641 move to head 675 and 679-681).

This is test code only. It asserts the expected workflow YAML text and does not itself change runtime provider behavior. No provider threat assets are directly affected: A-001, A-003, A-015, A-016, A-017, T-041 (the prefix-cache env pins at base lines 682-687 are test fixtures only), T-013 and T-054.

Limits:
- The actual workflow YAML files (provider-tests.yml, ci-master.yml, ci-dev.yml, provider-plan.yml) and the action.yml files were not supplied. Whether the workflows really implement these asserted conditions, and whether the git hardening covers every git-executed path, needs review in those files.
- Two gaps remain open in VALIDATE_GIT: the include-key regex may miss other exec-capable config keys (for example core.sshCommand, or filter/diff drivers), and gitattributes/info files were not considered. These are CI hardening concerns, not regressions from the base.
- The head ranges at lines 1089-1118 and 1335-1407 were not visible in these units.
